brief_summary: In this study we examine whether inducing insulin resistance by dexamethasone in healthy volunteers will lead to a decreased insulinotropic effect of the hormones GLP-1 and GIP.
brief_title: Insulinotropic Effect of GLP-1 and GIP After Dexamethasone

eligibility.criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Caucasians above 20 and below 45 years of age
* Normal glucose tolerance as assessed by the WHO criteria
* First degree relative and at least 1 second degree relative with type 2 diabetes
* Normal haemoglobin
* Informed consent

Exclusion Criteria:

* Liver disease (ALAT/ASAT \> 2 times normal value)
* Kidney disease (S-creatinin \> 130uM and/or albuminuria)
* Heart disease (NYHA II, III or IV)
* Treatment with medicine that cannot be paused
* Pregnancy of breast feeding

official_title: Loss of Insulinotropic Properties of Glucagon-like Peptide-1 (GLP-1) and Glucose-dependent Insulinotropic Peptide (GIP) After Glucocorticoid Induced Insulin Resistance

primary_outcomes.measure: The potentiating effects of GLP-1 on second phase insulin response when clamped at at bloodsugar of 7 mmol/l
